extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, appellate counsel, and patent law practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards for assessing Article III jurisdiction and remedies (mootness, standing, vacatur) in inter partes review appeals and parallel patent litigation. Focuses on voluntary cessation, covenants/disavowals, injury-in-fact, preclusion doctrines, and the Munsingwear/vacatur framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary cessation doctrine / burden to show conduct will not recur
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant claiming that its voluntary compliance moots a case 'bears the formidable burden of showing that it is absolutely clear the allegedly wrongful behavior could not reasonably be expected to recur.' (citing Already v. Nike and Friends of the Earth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial burden on the defendant to demonstrate that the allegedly wrongful conduct cannot reasonably be expected to recur; if defendant meets that burden, the plaintiff must then show it 'engages in or has sufficiently concrete plans to engage in activities not covered by' the defendant’s covenant/disavowal. Example: Nike’s broad covenant satisfied the defendant’s burden because it 'allow[ed] Already to produce all of its existing footwear designs . . . and any ‘colorable imitation’ of those designs.' (Already).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covenant/disavowal must be coextensive with asserted injury
rubrics_metrics.description: A covenant not to sue or a disavowal of appeal only moots a case when it is 'coextensive with the asserted injury' such that it 'encompasse[s] all of its allegedly unlawful conduct' tied to the plaintiff’s asserted injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the covenant/disavowal covers the full scope of the plaintiff’s claimed injury (e.g., existing products and foreseeable variants). If it is broad enough, the court may find the voluntary cessation test satisfied; if narrow, plaintiff may still show ongoing injury. See Already (covent broad enough) and this case (Cytonome disavowal treated as coextensive with ABS’s asserted injury).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff’s burden after defendant shows cessation (concrete plans test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a defendant shows its disavowal/covenant covers the allegedly wrongful conduct, the plaintiff must 'indicate that it engages in or has sufficiently concrete plans to engage in activities not covered by the [disavowal].' (Already).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because information about future business activities is uniquely within the plaintiff’s possession, the plaintiff must provide evidence of concrete, specific plans that would expose it to infringement liability (not mere generalized plans or litigation history). General assertions or non-specific plans are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article III injury-in-fact for potential infringement claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on potential infringement liability as injury-in-fact, a party 'must establish that it has concrete plans for future activity that creates a substantial risk of future infringement or [will] likely cause the patentee to assert a claim of infringement.' (JTEKT Corp.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must show concrete and imminent injury: finalized or concrete product plans, a substantial risk the product will infringe, or likelihood the patentee will sue. Mere competition, product concepts, or speculative R&D are insufficient. See JTEKT and GE v. UTC for examples of insufficient evidence (speculative or unfinalized products; no causal link to lost bids or costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for proving competitive/economic injury tied to a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive or economic harms are too speculative to confer standing absent concrete linkage to the patent (e.g., lost bids, demonstrable costs to design around, or concrete plans to use claimed features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations of generalized R&D expense or assertions that a patent 'hampered' development are insufficient without accounting or evidence tying the costs or lost opportunities directly to the patent. Courts require factual nexus (e.g., lost contract opportunities attributable to patent) — see General Electric and related decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kessler doctrine / preclusion effect of final noninfringement judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A final district-court judgment of noninfringement gives the accused devices 'a status as noninfringing devices,' barring the patentee from asserting that they infringe the same patent claims a second time (Kessler doctrine as applied in Brain Life, SpeedTrack, MGA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where final judgment in district court determined noninfringement (and claims could have been or were asserted), the patentee is estopped from relitigating infringement against essentially the same products; this reduces the plaintiff’s (patentee’s) ability to threaten renewed suit and thus bears on mootness/standing in related proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on Fort James exception to mootness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fort James does not create a broad patent-specific exception to mootness across parallel proceedings; it is an application of Cardinal Chemical concerning unresolved issues within the same proceeding (e.g., a post-verdict covenant does not moot collateral counterclaims in the same suit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fort James is limited to situations where a covenant post-verdict in the same proceeding cannot moot a separate counterclaim because the court retains jurisdiction to resolve issues (e.g., unenforceability) beyond the infringement finding. It does not extend to making an IPR appeal live where a final judgment of noninfringement in a separate proceeding and a disavowal remove any reasonable basis for future suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Munsingwear / vacatur doctrine for moot appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordinary practice is to vacate (Munsingwear) the judgment below when an appeal becomes moot through happenstance or the unilateral action of the prevailing party, to 'clear the path for future relitigation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacatur is an equitable remedy and 'the duty of the appellate court' in many cases; it is appropriate when the appellee’s unilateral action moots an appeal, unless mootness results from settlement or other equities counsel against vacatur. Courts may grant vacatur sua sponte and consider whether the losing party was prevented from obtaining review through no fault of its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture and equitable considerations in requesting vacatur
rubrics_metrics.description: A party’s failure to timely request vacatur (e.g., in reply briefs) may lead to forfeiture of the vacatur claim, though appellate courts retain equitable power to order vacatur despite forfeiture in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and preservation matter: courts have denied vacatur when request first raised at oral argument, especially in preliminary-injunction contexts; but other circuits and dissenting opinions recognize courts can and should issue vacatur sua sponte when fairness and Munsingwear principles require it (see Columbian Rope, Penguin Books). Courts weigh whether the mootness arose from the appellee’s unilateral action and the equities of leaving the lower ruling intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden-shifting dynamic and uniqueness of business-information possession
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a defendant shows its covenant/disavowal covers the challenged conduct, the burden shifts to the plaintiff to show concrete plans or ongoing activity not covered by the covenant; the court recognizes 'information about [the plaintiff’s] business activities and plans is uniquely within its possession.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shifts evidentiary burden practically: the plaintiff must come forward with specific evidence (product plans, timelines, designs) demonstrating risk not addressed by the covenant. Vague affidavits asserting only that new products or redesigns are planned without showing they would fall outside the covenant are insufficient (Already).
